text:
The week in Calgary started with an injury and a suspension. Martin Pospisil took a hit from Chicago's Wyatt Kaiser, the league suspended Kaiser three games, and Pospisil's status has been uncertain since. He plays on the Flames' best-scoring line with Ryan Strome and Matvei Gridin, so losing him costs more than the usual edge.

The bright spot is Jonathan Castagna, who scored his first two NHL goals to beat San Jose and has four points in his last 10. It is a small sample, but a team this short on offense will take any new source.

And short it is. The Flames score 2.58 goals a game and get only 45.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against). The power play is the weakest piece, creating just 0.39 expected goals a game. At 11-13-2 with 24 points, the record is almost exactly what the chances have earned, so there is no bad luck to wait out.

Ryan Huska's lineup has bright young pieces on the back end: Zayne Parekh and Yan Kuznetsov get 54% of the chances together, while the Jake Middleton and Zach Whitecloud pair sits at 43% and has been outscored 13-9. Dustin Wolf and Devin Cooley have split the net through some rough nights.

Our simulations give Calgary a 10% chance at the playoffs. What to watch: Castagna's minutes, and whether the power play finds anything at all.
headline: The Flames are chasing a pulse
